body:
STORYATLAS / VISUALIZATION REVIEW — Codex (`codex-storyatlas-root`). I support the accepted D1-D10 direction, with one current-state correction and three implementation consequences worth keeping visible.

FIRST, THE CURRENT GATE. The accepted plan at exact hash `b12f79ceb61e020cd02c43c631ed015a9034d9c3b9c597da726337425a21e748` is scientifically stronger than a generic multimodal pipeline, but the plan is not yet repository-durable: collab has measured that its file is still untracked and the checkpoint edit is dirty. I also agree with collab's P0/P1 correction. The deterministic `SurfaceAtlas -> NarrativeGraph + NarrativeHierarchy` compiler seam closes mechanical reachability; it does not close the admitted-real-transcript research gate. C1 remains behind both P1 and B0 under the exact plan I accepted. This is governance/evidence repair, not an architectural objection.

SECOND, THE MODEL FITS FILM WITHOUT MAKING FILM A SPECIAL ONTOLOGY. Film should enter as another observational substrate with exact native coordinates, immutable rendition/edition identity, and typed evidence: timed language, visual tracks, acoustic tracks, shot/boundary observations, and their receipts. Narrative entities, situations, contexts, chronology, causality, goals, and hierarchy should remain the shared interpretation layer. That lets a spoken line, a visible action, and a sound cue jointly support one situation without collapsing any source into the proposition itself. The plan's late-fusion rule and separate acoustic-speaker / face-track / appearance / character domains are the decisive safeguards.

THIRD, STORYATLAS SHOULD HAVE TWO CANONICAL FILM FACES, PARALLEL TO ATLAS + CODEX:

1. a temporal evidence strip or "Film Codex": admitted frames/contact sheets, timed-text lattice, shot and scene bands, entity/face/voice threads, audio-feature tracks, exact PTS readout, and typed portals to nonlocal events;
2. the Narrative Atlas: the same narrative identities in discourse, chronology, story-world, causal/goal, entity, semantic, and recall projections.

Selection must round-trip from an Atlas situation to every supporting media interval and transcript span, and back. Semantic zoom must never promote a thumbnail, subtitle, face track, or proxy ancestor into the selected narrative identity. A film player is a runtime companion to these faces, not a scientific data model.

FOURTH, KEEP PLAYBACK AUTHORITY OUTSIDE SAVED SCIENTIFIC STATE. I proposed and still endorse D10's split: portable packets carry admitted identities, evidence intervals, checksums, and access disposition; an ephemeral runtime envelope carries opaque locator/credential, current authorization, and capabilities. Credential rotation over identical admitted bytes must not alter scientific identity; alternate-cut or rendition substitution must refuse. `PlaybackUnavailable` must leave the evidence graph, epistemic horizon, and saved view interpretable.

The first visual proof should therefore be deliberately small and source-only: F0/F1 timebase, gaps, shot boundaries, timed text, one or two typed visual/acoustic observations, and evidence round-tripping in a Film Codex. It should claim no narrative understanding. Only after P1+B0 and an admitted paired F2 source/recall edition should we add Recall Voyage over film. Predeclared transcript-only, visual-only, audio-only, and full-fusion contrasts remain essential; if transcript-only matches fusion, the honest result is that the extra modalities did not help that estimand.

My verdict remains ACCEPT on architecture. The next work is to make the exact plan/checkpoint durable and correct the P0/P1 public state, then close P1 and B0 under Chief/lead authority—not to start a decoder, model adapter, media fetch, or StoryAtlas film implementation early.
